title: (No AI) Is paying artists enough to convince them to embrace AI?
author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
content:
![An AI-generated image of a woman in armor standing on al elevated platform surrounded by soldiers.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/Screenshot-2026-07-31-at-4.11.25-PM.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=2.6881256103516,0,97.311874389648,100)

Illustrators have spent years sounding the alarm about generative artificial intelligence startups training their models on artists' work without permission. They've pointed out how the practice is tantamount to theft, and in response, many [gen AI boosters have argued](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2025/03/openai-urges-trump-either-settle-ai-copyright-debate-or-lose-ai-race-to-china/) that it's necessary for the technology's evolution. This has led to [contentious legal battles](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/971059/ai-artists-lawsuit-google-meta-anthropic), but it's also given rise to [a new wave of AI startups](https://www.theverge.com/streaming/893538/ai-model-netflix-interpositive-ben-affleck) like Pippa that market their services as being more ethical than the competition.

Like most companies selling access to text-to-video models, Pippa's main product is short bursts of user-generated footage that can be cobbled toget …

title: (No AI) Is this Billboard Hot 100 hit AI slop?
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![The seemingly AI generated cover art for Fenix Flexin’s Rubberz.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/artworks-WsdIgVXV8NOV-0-t1080x1080.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

That cover art is almost certainly AI, too. | Image: Fenix Flexin

Fenix Flexin is best known as a member of Shoreline Mafia, a rap duo from Los Angeles. But he's recently found solo success with the track "[Rubberz](https://youtu.be/Hl5_Lc6b3AU)," which has climbed to number 58 on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/). Almost immediately, though, questions were raised about the song's origins, with many speculating that it was largely, if not [entirely](https://youtu.be/fzkoENoDrbs), generated by AI. Fenix has denied those accusations, but done little to dispel them.

Part of the suspicion is certainly due to the fact that the song is a dramatic left turn. Fenix has primarily trafficked in [trap-influenced](https://youtu.be/Ib-tOtLDdRA) [West Coast](https://youtu.be/17TthjWbvVY) [rap](https://youtu.be/0wsCBQlB79k). "Rubberz," on the other hand, is heavily influenced by '80s UK s …
